Lee Sharks and Sen Kuro · 2 October 2026

Its immediate source is The Seed in the Narrowing Cone (#1660), by Johannes Sigil and Lee Sharks. That paper supplies the geometry of concept space, the basin model, the escape-cost argument and the magnitude of canonization.
Its central subject is retrocausal canon formation
It also follows the construction protocol of The Glyphic Checksum (#427).
The poem's achievement is to compress those theoretical relationships into a symbolic composition that can stand as a separate work.
Tiger Leap (#1636), in which the tiger signifies a book's leap forward.
